phytase addition improves phytate, AA, and energy digestibility in broiler chickens fed corn-based diets at all dietary Ca:Av P ratios.
increasing dietary Ca:AvPsupplementation with phytase improved energy, amino acid, and phytate digestibility and decreased ileal digesta pH in broilers.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary Ca:Av P ratio and phytate supplementation on ileal phytic acid degradation, AA digestibility, and bone ash of broilers fed a corn-based diet.
the effects of dietary calcium to available phosphorus ratio and phytate degradation on nutrient digestibility in corn-based diets for broiler chickens.
the use of phytase in broiler diets to reduce the negative effects of high dietary Ca levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phytase addition improved nutrient digestibility at all dietary Ca:Av P ratios evaluated in the current experiment.

the addition of 1,000 units phytase/kg of feed improved phytate degradation (by up to 50%) and nutrient digestibility at all dietary Ca:Avp ratios evaluated in this work, and it is recommended that phytase should be included in corn-based diets for broilers at a level of 1,500 units phytase per kg of feed.
the effect of Ca:Avp ratio on phytate degradation was not significant, whereas phytase supplementation increased phytate degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
increasing the Ca:AvP in corn-based diets from 1.43 to 3.57 significantly decreased phytate degradation in the ileum, P digestibility, bone ash, WG, FI, FCR, and gizzard pH.
increasing the dietary Ca:Avp ratio from 1.43 to 3.57 decreased WG, FI, FCR, and phytate degradation in broilers fed diets without added phytase, but had no effect in diets with added phytase.
the addition of phytase to corn-based diets can improve the digestibility of P and AA at all dietary Ca:Av P ratios evaluated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phytase addition improved nutrient digestibility in diets with low and high Ca:AvP, but the improvement was greater in diets with low Ca:AvP.
the addition of phytase to diets with low Ca:AvP can improve P utilization and AA digestibility.
phytate degradation was significantly reduced by increasing Ca:AvP. However, phytase supplementation can counteract the negative effect of Ca on phytate degradation.
